question:
Which of the following is the basic function of a computer?

[MPPCS (J) 2019]
options: input
storage
processing
All of these
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is All of these

Explanation:
The basic function of a computer is Input, Processing, Output, and Storage, known as the IPO cycle. Input involves receiving data, Processing involves manipulating that data, Output displays the results, and Storage saves data for future use. All these functions are essential for computer operation. The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is the main component for processing, while Memory and Storage Devices assist in data storage. Input Devices like keyboards and mice, and Output Devices like monitors and printers, complete this cycle.

Extra Facts:
In computer architecture, the Von Neumann Architecture is fundamental, based on the concept of input, processing, output, and storage. The Operating System manages these functions. The combination of hardware and software enables the computer to perform tasks. Networking and Database systems enhance data processing and storage, making computers crucial in modern technology.

Explanation:
कंप्यूटर का मूल कार्य इनपुट, प्रोसेसिंग, आउटपुट और स्टोरेज है, जिसे IPO चक्र के रूप में जाना जाता है। इनपुट डेटा प्राप्त करना है, प्रोसेसिंग उस डेटा को प्रोसेस करना है, आउटपुट परिणाम दिखाना है, और स्टोरेज डेटा को भविष्य के लिए सहेजना है। ये सभी कार्य कंप्यूटर के संचालन के लिए आवश्यक हैं। सेंट्रल प्रोसेसिंग यूनिट (CPU) प्रोसेसिंग का मुख्य भाग है, जबकि मेमोरी और स्टोरेज डिवाइस डेटा संग्रहण में सहायता करते हैं। इनपुट डिवाइस जैसे कीबोर्ड और माउस, और आउटपुट डिवाइस जैसे मॉनिटर और प्रिंटर, इस चक्र को पूरा करते हैं।

Extra Facts:

question:
Which of the following is/are NOT valid characteristics of a computer system?

[NVS Junior Secretariat Assistant 09.03.2022 (Shift-I)]
options: (i) IQ (ii) Accountability
(i) and (iv)
(iii) and (iv)
(i) and (ii)
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Option 4 - (i) and (ii)

Explanation:
The fundamental characteristics of a computer system are Speed, Accuracy, Reliability, Storage Capacity, Diligence, and Versatility. IQ (Intelligence Quotient) and Accountability are not characteristics of a computer. IQ is a human attribute related to cognitive abilities, while Accountability is an ethical or social concept that applies to humans or organizations, not machines. A computer is a machine; it does not possess the ability to make independent moral judgments or be held accountable for its actions. Therefore, both of these are NOT valid characteristics of a computer system.

Extra Facts:
Understanding computer characteristics is a crucial part of computer fundamentals. Speed is measured in nanoseconds and picoseconds. Accuracy means the computer provides error-free results, provided the input and program are correct. Reliability refers to the ability to work consistently for long periods. Storage Capacity is the power to store vast amounts of data and information, measured in bytes. Diligence means performing monotonous tasks without getting tired. Versatility is the capability to perform different types of tasks. Computers lack emotions, intelligence, and self-awareness, which are inherently human traits.

question:
CPU is also called

[UPPCL TG-2 3/11/2023 (Shift-II)]
options: semi-processor
miniprocessor
microprocessor
multi-processor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is microprocessor

Explanation:
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is commonly referred to as a microprocessor because modern CPUs are built on a single integrated circuit (IC) chip. A microprocessor is a programmable device that handles all arithmetic, logical, and control operations of a computer. It is considered the 'brain' of the computer and integrates components like the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and CU (Control Unit). Other options like semi-processor, miniprocessor, or multi-processor are not standard terms for CPU.

Extra Facts:
The development of the microprocessor began in the 1970s with the Intel 4004. Modern microprocessors use multi-core technology, where multiple processing units are on a single chip. They operate at clock speeds in the GHz (gigahertz) range and are equipped with cache memory to enhance processing speed. Microprocessors are used not only in computers but also in smartphones, embedded systems, and IoT devices.

Extra Facts:
माइक्रोप्रोसेसर का विकास 1970 के दशक में इंटेल 4004 के साथ शुरू हुआ। आधुनिक माइक्रोप्रोसेसर मल्टी-कोर टेक्नोलॉजी का उपयोग करते हैं, जहाँ एक ही चिप पर कई प्रोसेसिंग यूनिट्स होती हैं। ये GHz (गीगाहर्ट्ज) रेंज में क्लॉक स्पीड पर काम करते हैं और कैश मेमोरी से लैस होते हैं जो प्रोसेसिंग गति बढ़ाती है। माइक्रोप्रोसेसर न केवल कंप्यूटरों में, बल्कि स्मार्टफोन्स, एम्बेडेड सिस्टम्स और IoT डिवाइसेज में भी उपयोग किए जाते हैं।

question:
For computer, world consists of zeros and ones only. To store the zeros and ones, ........... is placed inside a processor:

[(UPPCL TG2 11-11-2016)]
options: I/O device
Instruction set
Transistor
Main Memory
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Transistor

Explanation:
Computers operate on the binary system, using only 0s and 1s (bits). Inside a processor, transistors are used to store and process these bits. A transistor is a semiconductor device that can act as a switch, being either ON (representing 1) or OFF (representing 0). Millions or billions of transistors combine to form integrated circuits, which are the core components of a processor. I/O devices and main memory are located outside the processor, while an instruction set is a collection of software commands, not a hardware component for data storage.

Extra Facts:
Transistors form the logic gates (AND, OR, NOT) that are the foundation of all computations and decisions in computers. Moore's Law states that the number of transistors on a processor doubles approximately every two years. Modern CPUs contain billions of transistors built using nanometer-scale technology. Without transistors, the digital revolution would not have been possible, as they are fundamental to microprocessors and memory chips.

question:
What is used to receive control signals between the processor and other devices?

[UPPCL Office Assistant III 24-10-2018 (Evening)]
options: LCD
Joystick
MICR
Control Bus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Control Bus

Explanation:
The Control Bus is used in computer systems to receive control signals between the processor and other devices. It is a crucial component of the computer's system bus, working alongside the data bus and address bus. The Control Bus manages the flow of instructions and ensures that various hardware components operate at the right time and in the correct sequence. It transmits essential control signals such as read/write signals, interrupt signals, and clock signals, enabling coordinated operation of the computer system.

Extra Facts:
The computer system bus consists of three main components: data bus (for data transfer), address bus (for specifying memory addresses), and control bus (for managing control signals). The control bus is bidirectional, meaning signals can flow in both directions. It facilitates communication between the CPU and I/O devices and affects the system's overall performance. In modern computer architecture, bus speed and width are key factors determining a computer's processing capability and efficiency.

Control Bus कंप्यूटर सिस्टम में प्रोसेसर और अन्य उपकरणों के बीच कंट्रोल सिग्नलों के आदान-प्रदान के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है। यह कंप्यूटर के सिस्टम बस का एक महत्वपूर्ण भाग है, जो डेटा बस और एड्रेस बस के साथ मिलकर काम करता है। Control Bus निर्देशों के प्रवाह को नियंत्रित करता है और यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि विभिन्न हार्डवेयर घटक सही समय पर और सही क्रम में कार्य करें। यह रीड/राइट सिग्नल, इंटरप्ट सिग्नल, और क्लॉक सिग्नल जैसे महत्वपूर्ण नियंत्रण संकेतों को प्रसारित करता है, जिससे कंप्यूटर का समन्वित संचालन संभव हो पाता है।

Extra Facts:
कंप्यूटर सिस्टम बस तीन प्रमुख घटकों से मिलकर बनी होती है: डेटा बस (डेटा स्थानांतरण के लिए), एड्रेस बस (मेमोरी एड्रेस निर्दिष्ट करने के लिए), और कंट्रोल बस (नियंत्रण सिग्नल प्रबंधन के लिए)। कंट्रोल बस बाइडायरेक्शनल होती है, जिसका अर्थ है कि सिग्नल दोनों दिशाओं में प्रवाहित हो सकते हैं। यह CPU और I/O उपकरणों के बीच संचार को सुगम बनाती है और सिस्टम के समग्र प्रदर्शन को प्रभावित करती है। आधुनिक कंप्यूटर आर्किटेक्चर में, बस की गति और चौड़ाई कंप्यूटर की प्रसंस्करण क्षमता का निर्धारण करने वाले प्रमुख कारक हैं।

question:
Which among the following has capability to execute computer's command?

[(UPPCL TG2 11-11-2016)]
options: Processor Socket
Main Memory
Arithmetic Logic Unit
Cache Memory
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Arithmetic Logic Unit

Explanation:
The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) is a core component of the computer's Central Processing Unit (CPU) that possesses the capability to execute all arithmetic and logical operations. When a command is given to the computer, the ALU actually performs the calculations and comparisons to execute that command. The Processor Socket only connects the CPU to the motherboard, Main Memory temporarily stores data and instructions, and Cache Memory provides fast data access for the CPU - but the actual execution of commands is performed exclusively by the ALU.

Extra Facts:
The ALU plays a crucial role in the computer architecture's Instruction Cycle. It becomes active during the 'Execute' phase of the Fetch, Decode, Execute cycle. ALU operates on the binary number system and can perform various types of microoperations. Modern CPUs may contain multiple ALUs that enable parallel processing. The functionality of ALU directly impacts the computer's overall performance capability.

Extra Facts:
ALU कंप्यूटर आर्किटेक्चर में निर्देश चक्र (Instruction Cycle) का महत्वपूर्ण भाग है। यह Fetch, Decode, Execute चक्र के 'Execute' चरण में सक्रिय होता है। ALU बाइनरी संख्या प्रणाली पर काम करता है और विभिन्न प्रकार के माइक्रोऑपरेशन कर सकता है। आधुनिक CPU में एक से अधिक ALU हो सकते हैं जो पैरेलल प्रोसेसिंग को सक्षम बनाते हैं। ALU की कार्यक्षमता कंप्यूटर की समग्र प्रदर्शन क्षमता को सीधे प्रभावित करती है।

question:
Control Unit is called the......... of a computer.

[SSC JE Electrical (Exam date 27.01.2018) Shift-I]
options: heart
nerve center or brain
Kidney
All options are correct.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is nerve center or brain

Explanation:
The Control Unit is called the 'nerve center or brain' of a computer because it is a core component of the Central Processing Unit (CPU). It controls and coordinates all operations of the computer. The Control Unit fetches instructions from memory, decodes them, and then sends signals to other components like the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and registers for execution. It ensures that data reaches the right place at the right time, much like the human brain controls various parts of the body. It is the central controller of the computer's Fetch-Decode-Execute Cycle.

Extra Facts:
The CPU primarily consists of three components: the Control Unit (CU), Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), and Registers. The ALU performs all arithmetic and logical calculations. Together, the Control Unit and ALU act as the 'brain' of the computer. Computer memory is of two types: Primary (RAM, ROM) and Secondary (HDD, SSD). The function of the Control Unit is to manage the flow of data between primary memory and the CPU.

In embedded systems, microcontrollers are classified into various types based on their architecture, bit-size, and applications. Among the given options, Only A is correct because it represents a valid type of microcontroller, while option B indicates an invalid or incorrect category. Microcontrollers like 8051, PIC, ARM, and AVR are widely used in embedded systems. These are single-chip computers integrating CPU, RAM, ROM, and I/O ports, making them ideal for automotive, medical devices, and IoT equipment.

Extra Facts:
The main difference between a microcontroller and a microprocessor is that microcontrollers have all components integrated on a single chip, whereas microprocessors require external components. Microcontrollers with Harvard architecture (e.g., PIC) have separate data and instruction memory, enhancing performance. Those with RISC architecture (e.g., ARM) offer low power consumption and high efficiency, making them dominant in mobile devices.

question:
Which of the following control memory input and output devices?

[(UPSSSC JE-2016)]
options: C.P.U.
A.L.U.
C.U.
Memory
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is C.P.U.

Explanation:
The C.P.U. (Central Processing Unit) is the primary component of a computer that controls all data processing operations. It coordinates between memory, input devices (like keyboard, mouse), and output devices (like monitor, printer). The CPU uses its Control Unit (C.U.) to decode instructions and send control signals to all devices. The A.L.U. (Arithmetic Logic Unit) only performs arithmetic and logical operations, while memory handles data storage. Therefore, complete control over input-output and memory management is exercised by the CPU.

Extra Facts:
The CPU is often called the 'brain' of the computer, operating on the fetch-decode-execute cycle. The Control Unit is a part of the CPU that generates timing and control signals. Memory is divided into primary (RAM) and secondary (HDD/SSD). Input/Output devices establish communication between the computer and the external world. The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects all components.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Switched Mode Power Supply

Explanation:
SMPS stands for Switched Mode Power Supply. It is a power supply unit that uses high-frequency switching transistors to efficiently convert electrical power. It works by converting AC current to DC current and is widely used in electronic devices like computers, televisions, and mobile chargers. The key features of SMPS include - high efficiency, compact size, low heat generation, and wide input voltage range. It is more energy efficient compared to linear power supplies because it regulates power through switching transistors.

Extra Facts:
Power Supply Unit (PSU) is a critical component of computer systems that ensures stable power supply to the motherboard, hard disk, and other peripherals. SMPS involves processes of rectification, filtering, and regulation. Modern SMPS use PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) technology which further enhances power efficiency. Computer PSUs provide different voltage outputs (+3.3V, +5V, +12V) and also offer protection features like overvoltage/undervoltage protection.

question:
What does CMOS stand for?

[NVS PGT 19.09.2019 (Shift-I)]
options: Core Memory Oriented Semiconductor
Core Memory Offset Semiconductor
Capacitive Metal Oxidised Semiconductor
Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor

Explanation:
CMOS stands for Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor, which is a type of semiconductor technology used in integrated circuits. The key characteristic of CMOS technology is its low power consumption since it only uses power during switching operations. In computer systems, CMOS is primarily used to store BIOS settings, which are maintained by a CMOS battery. This technology is widely employed in microprocessors, memory chips, and other digital logic circuits due to its efficiency and reliability in modern computing devices.

Extra Facts:
CMOS technology utilizes complementary pairs of NMOS and PMOS transistors, enhancing power efficiency. It forms the foundation of VLSI design and plays a crucial role in the development of modern microprocessors. CMOS chips generate less heat and allow for high-density circuit integration. In computers, information such as time, date, and hardware configuration is stored in CMOS, maintained by battery backup, ensuring data persistence even when the system is powered off.

CMOS का पूरा नाम Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor (पूरक धातु ऑक्साइड सेमी कंडक्टर) है। यह एक प्रकार का सेमीकंडक्टर टेक्नोलॉजी है जिसका उपयोग इंटीग्रेटेड सर्किट में किया जाता है। CMOS तकनीक की मुख्य विशेषता इसकी कम बिजली की खपत है, क्योंकि यह केवल स्विचिंग के समय ही बिजली का उपयोग करता है। कंप्यूटर सिस्टम में CMOS का सबसे महत्वपूर्ण उपयोग BIOS सेटिंग्स को स्टोर करने के लिए होता है, जो CMOS बैटरी द्वारा संचालित होता है। यह तकनीक माइक्रोप्रोसेसर, मेमोरी चिप्स और अन्य डिजिटल लॉजिक सर्किट्स में व्यापक रूप से प्रयोग की जाती है।

Extra Facts:
CMOS तकनीक NMOS और PMOS ट्रांजिस्टर के पूरक जोड़े का उपयोग करती है, जिससे शक्ति दक्षता में सुधार होता है। यह VLSI डिजाइन का आधार है और आधुनिक माइक्रोप्रोसेसर के विकास में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है। CMOS चिप्स कम गर्मी उत्पन्न करते हैं और उच्च घनत्व वाले सर्किट की अनुमति देते हैं। कंप्यूटर के BIOS में समय, तारीख और हार्डवेयर कॉन्फ़िगरेशन जैसी जानकारी CMOS में स्टोर रहती है, जो बैटरी बैकअप द्वारा बनाए रखी जाती है।

question:
The maximum memory size of third generation microprocessor is

[BPSC TRE 2.0 Exam-2023 (11-12)]
options: 4 GB
16 MB
16 GB
More than one of the above
None of the above
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 4 GB

Explanation:
Third-generation microprocessors (like Intel 80386) used a 32-bit address bus, which can access 2³² = 4,294,967,296 memory locations. Since each location typically stores 1 byte, the maximum memory size is 4 GB (4,294,967,296 bytes). This was a significant milestone in computer architecture, as it enabled virtual memory and multitasking capabilities. 16 MB and 16 GB are incorrect because 16 MB was characteristic of the second generation (24-bit addressing), and 16 GB relates to the fourth generation (36-bit addressing).

Extra Facts:
Microprocessor generations are based on transistor technology and address bus width. The first generation (4-bit) supported a few KB, second (8-bit) up to 64 KB, third (32-bit) up to 4 GB, and fourth (64-bit) up to 16 EB (exabytes). The Pentium processor (1995) introduced 36-bit addressing supporting 64 GB memory. The Memory Management Unit (MMU) enabled virtual memory, which is fundamental to modern operating systems.

question:
To measure the speed of a processor, ........... is used.

[Allahabad High Court (ARO) 20/12/2021 (Shift-II)]
options: Processing speed
Clock speed
Memory
Unit
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Clock speed

Explanation:
The speed of a processor is measured using clock speed, which is measured in Hertz (Hz). It represents the speed of the processor's internal clock cycle, determining how many instructions the processor can execute per second. Modern processors operate in Gigahertz (GHz), where 1 GHz = 1 billion cycles per second. Higher clock speed means faster performance, but it alone doesn't determine overall processor capability - number of cores, cache memory, and architecture also play crucial roles.

Extra Facts:
Besides clock speed, processor performance is also affected by cores (dual-core, quad-core), cache memory (L1, L2, L3), and instruction set architecture (CISC, RISC). Multi-core processors handle multiple tasks simultaneously, while hyper-threading allows each physical core to run more than one thread. Overclocking can increase clock speed but may cause heat and stability issues.

question:
This bus usually a set of wires that links the CPU to the RAM (and to other places). If the CPU want to fetch an instruction from a particular location in RAM, or want to write piece of data to a particular location in RAM, it put the specific location details on this bus.

[UPPCL TG-2 17/11/2023 (Shift-I)]
options: Control Bus
Communication Bus
Data Bus
Address Bus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Address Bus

Explanation:
The Address Bus is a unidirectional bus that connects the CPU to memory (RAM) and I/O devices. When the CPU needs to read or write data from a specific memory location, it sends the address of that location on the Address Bus. This bus is connected to the Memory Address Register (MAR) and determines the system's memory addressability. For example, a 32-bit address bus can address 2^32 (4 GB) of memory. It is distinct from the Control Bus and Data Bus, which are used for control signals and actual data transfer respectively.

Extra Facts:
Computer systems have three main buses: Address Bus (specifies memory location), Data Bus (for data transfer), and Command/Control Bus (for control signals). Bus architecture affects computer performance. The width of the address bus directly impacts the memory address space. Modern computers use system bus or Front Side Bus (FSB) that connects CPU to Northbridge. PCI bus is a popular expansion bus that connects peripheral devices to the motherboard.

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है एड्रेस बस

Explanation:
एड्रेस बस एक यूनिडायरेक्शनल बस है जो CPU को मेमोरी (RAM) और I/O डिवाइस से जोड़ती है। जब CPU को किसी विशिष्ट मेमोरी लोकेशन से डेटा पढ़ना या लिखना होता है, तो वह एड्रेस बस पर उस लोकेशन का एड्रेस भेजता है। यह बस मेमोरी एड्रेस रजिस्टर (MAR) से जुड़ी होती है और सिस्टम की मेमोरी एड्रेसेबिलिटी निर्धारित करती है। उदाहरण के लिए, 32-बिट एड्रेस बस 2^32 (4 GB) मेमोरी एड्रेस कर सकती है। यह कंट्रोल बस और डेटा बस से अलग है, जो क्रमशः कंट्रोल सिग्नल और एक्चुअल डेटा ट्रांसफर के लिए उपयोग होती हैं।

Extra Facts:
कंप्यूटर सिस्टम में तीन मुख्य बसें होती हैं: एड्रेस बस (मेमोरी लोकेशन स्पेसिफाई करती है), डेटा बस (डेटा ट्रांसफर के लिए), और कमांड/कंट्रोल बस (कंट्रोल सिग्नल के लिए)। बस आर्किटेक्चर कंप्यूटर के परफॉर्मेंस को प्रभावित करता है। एड्रेस बस की चौड़ाई सीधे मेमोरी एड्रेस स्पेस को प्रभावित करती है। आधुनिक कंप्यूटरों में सिस्टम बस या फ्रंट साइड बस (FSB) का उपयोग होता है, जो CPU को नॉर्थब्रिज से जोड़ती है। PCI बस एक लोकप्रिय एक्सपांशन बस है जो पेरिफेरल डिवाइस को मदरबोर्ड से जोड़ती है।

question:
Which of the following is the core of the Linux system, manages the CPU, memory, and peripheral devices, and is the lowest level of the OS?

[UPPCL Executive Assistant 24-11-2022 Shift-II]
options: Bootloader
Desktop environment
Kernel
Daemons
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kernel

Explanation:
The core of the Linux system is the Kernel. It is the lowest level and main component of the operating system responsible for managing CPU, memory, and peripheral devices. The Kernel acts as an interface between hardware and software, provides system calls, and controls process scheduling, memory management, and device drivers. While Bootloader is responsible for system startup, Desktop environment provides user interface, and Daemons are background services - none of these form the core of the OS.

Extra Facts:
The Linux Kernel uses monolithic architecture where all OS services run in kernel space. It supports advanced features like multitasking, virtual memory, and networking. The Kernel forms the foundation for system security and resource allocation, and without it, no operating system can function. The Linux Kernel is open-source and was originally developed by Linus Torvalds. It handles interrupt management, process synchronization, and file system operations.

☛ What is called the heart of the operating system? → Kernel
☛ What is the Kernel of Windows OS? → NT Kernel

☛ Which program boots the computer? → Bootloader

Linux Kernel मोनोलिथिक आर्किटेक्चर का उपयोग करता है, जहाँ सभी OS सेवाएँ Kernel स्पेस में चलती हैं। यह मल्टीटास्किंग, वर्चुअल मेमोरी, और नेटवर्किंग जैसी एडवांस्ड फीचर्स सपोर्ट करता है। Kernel सिस्टम सुरक्षा और रिसोर्स आवंटन का आधार है, और इसके बिना कोई भी ऑपरेटिंग सिस्टम कार्य नहीं कर सकता। Linux Kernel ओपन-सोर्स है और इसे लिनुस टोरवाल्ड्स द्वारा विकसित किया गया था।

question:
ALU generally uses an accumulator to store operands and results. Which of the following options correctly describes the accumulator?

[UPPCL Executive Assistant 30-11-2022 Shift-I]
options: Register
Main memory
Processing unit
Secondary memory
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Register

Explanation:
An Accumulator is a special type of register located inside the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Its primary function is to temporarily store operands and hold the results of arithmetic and logical operations. Since registers are located directly inside the CPU, data access speed in them is much faster compared to Main Memory (RAM) or Secondary Memory (Hard Disk). It plays a crucial role in optimizing processor performance. Other options like Main Memory or Secondary Memory are slower and serve different purposes compared to an accumulator.

Extra Facts:
Registers are the smallest and fastest memory in the CPU, used for temporary storage of data and instructions. The Accumulator is a key register, but other important registers include the Program Counter (PC), Memory Address Register (MAR), and Instruction Register (IR). The ALU and Control Unit (CU) together form the Central Processing Unit (CPU). In the computer memory hierarchy, registers are at the top, having the highest speed and the smallest capacity.

Explanation:
एक संचायक (Accumulator) एक विशेष प्रकार का रजिस्टर है जो अंकगणितीय तर्क इकाई (ALU) के अंदर स्थित होता है। यह संकार्यों (Operands) को अस्थायी रूप से संग्रहीत करने और अंकगणितीय एवं तार्किक संक्रियाओं के परिणामों को धारण करने का कार्य करता है। चूंकि रजिस्टर सीधे CPU के अंदर स्थित होते हैं, इसलिए इनमें डेटा एक्सेस की गति मुख्य मेमोरी (RAM) या द्वितीयक मेमोरी (Hard Disk) की तुलना में बहुत अधिक होती है। यह प्रोसेसर के प्रदर्शन को अनुकूलित करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। अन्य विकल्प जैसे मुख्य मेमोरी या द्वितीयक मेमोरी, संचायक की तुलना में धीमी और अलग उद्देश्यों के लिए उपयोग की जाती हैं।

Extra Facts:
रजिस्टर CPU की सबसे छोटी और सबसे तेज मेमोरी हैं, जो डेटा और निर्देशों को अस्थायी रूप से संग्रहीत करते हैं। संचायक एक प्रमुख रजिस्टर है, लेकिन अन्य महत्वपूर्ण रजिस्टरों में प्रोग्राम काउंटर (PC), मेमोरी एड्रेस रजिस्टर (MAR), और इंस्ट्रक्शन रजिस्टर (IR) शामिल हैं। ALU और कंट्रोल यूनिट (CU) मिलकर सेंट्रल प्रोसेसिंग यूनिट (CPU) का निर्माण करते हैं। कंप्यूटर की मेमोरी पदानुक्रम में रजिस्टर सबसे ऊपर होते हैं, जिनकी गति सबसे अधिक और क्षमता सबसे कम होती है।

question:
A CPU has three parts.

[UPPCL APS 27-09-2018 (Evening)]
options: Control unit, disk drive, peripheral
ALU, control unit, memory
ALU, memory, chip
Chip, disk drive, peripheral
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is ALU, control unit, memory

Explanation:
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is often called the 'brain' of the computer. Its three primary components are the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), the Control Unit (CU), and Memory or Registers. The ALU performs all arithmetic calculations and logical operations. The Control Unit manages and coordinates the flow of data and instructions between all components of the computer. The Memory (Registers) temporarily stores the data and instructions that the CPU is currently processing. Disk drives and peripherals are not part of the CPU; they are external devices.

Extra Facts:
CPU speed is measured in Hertz (Hz). Modern CPUs are multi-core (e.g., dual-core, quad-core), meaning multiple processing units exist on a single chip. Cache memory is a special, extremely fast part of the CPU memory that stores frequently used data to speed up processing. The primary function of the CPU is to complete the Fetch, Decode, and Execute cycle, which is the fundamental process of a computer's operation.

question:
The set of wires, connecting the microprocessor and the memory, through which the data flows is called:

[UPPCL APS 27-09-2018 (Evening)]
options: memory
data wire
database
databus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is databus

Explanation:
The databus is a set of wires in a computer system that connects the microprocessor with memory and other peripheral devices for data transfer. It functions as a communication pathway allowing the CPU to exchange data with memory and input/output devices. The databus consists of parallel wires that can transfer multiple bits simultaneously. In computer architecture, the width of the databus significantly impacts system performance. While data wire refers to a single connection, databus represents an organized system of multiple wires working together to facilitate efficient data communication between components.

Extra Facts:
Computer systems typically have three main types of buses: data bus (for data transfer), address bus (for specifying memory locations), and control bus (for control signals). The databus width is measured in bits (such as 32-bit, 64-bit) and determines how much data can be transferred at once. Modern computers use high-speed bus architectures like PCI Express and USB. The bus architecture significantly influences a computer's overall performance and scalability, making it a critical component in system design and optimization.

solution:

Extra Facts:
The CPU has two main components: the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) and the CU (Control Unit). The ALU performs all arithmetic and logical operations, while the CU controls the flow of instructions between all other components of the computer. The speed of a CPU is measured in Hertz. Modern CPUs are multi-core, meaning there is more than one processor within a single chip, allowing for parallel processing and significantly increasing performance.

question:
Which bus is used to specify memory locations for the data being transferred?

[NVS PGT 19.09.2019 (Shift-I)]
options: Control bus
Data bus
Address bus
I/O bus
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Address bus

Explanation:
In computer systems, the address bus is used to specify memory locations for data being transferred. It is a unidirectional bus that carries address signals from the CPU to memory or I/O devices. When the CPU needs to read or write data from a specific memory location, it sends the address of that location on the address bus. The actual data transfer then occurs on the data bus. The width of the address bus determines the system's memory addressing capability - for example, a 32-bit address bus can address up to 4GB of memory.

Extra Facts:
Computer systems have three main buses: address bus (specifies memory locations), data bus (transfers actual data), and control bus (sends control signals). The bus architecture affects computer performance. The system bus connects the CPU to memory and other devices. Modern computers use advanced bus technologies like Front Side Bus (FSB) and QuickPath Interconnect. The clock speed and width of the bus determine the data transfer rate.

question:
Which is called as brain of any computer system?

[RRB NTPC 09.01.2021 (Shift-I) Stage Ist]
options: UPS
Monitor
ALU
CPU
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is CPU

Explanation:
The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is called the brain of any computer system because it controls and coordinates all operations of the computer. The CPU consists of three main components: the ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) which performs mathematical and logical operations, the Control Unit which decodes instructions and directs other components, and Registers that temporarily store data and instructions. It receives data from input devices, processes it, and sends results to output devices. A monitor is an output device, UPS is a power backup system, and ALU is merely a component of the CPU.

Extra Facts:
CPU performance is measured by clock speed (in Hertz). Modern CPUs are multi-core processors (dual-core, quad-core) that can work on multiple tasks simultaneously. Intel and AMD are leading CPU manufacturing companies. The CPU processes instructions through the machine cycle (fetch, decode, execute, store). Cache memory located inside the CPU increases data access speed. CPU development has occurred through generations (first to fifth).

Explanation:
सीपीयू (सेंट्रल प्रोसेसिंग यूनिट) को कंप्यूटर सिस्टम का मस्तिष्क कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह कंप्यूटर के सभी ऑपरेशन्स को कंट्रोल और कोऑर्डिनेट करता है। सीपीयू में तीन मुख्य भाग होते हैं: एएलयू (अर्थमैटिक लॉजिक यूनिट) जो गणितीय और तार्किक ऑपरेशन्स करता है, कंट्रोल यूनिट जो इंस्ट्रक्शन्स को डिकोड करके अन्य कंपोनेंट्स को निर्देश देती है, और रजिस्टर्स जो डेटा और इंस्ट्रक्शन्स को टेम्पररी स्टोर करते हैं। यह इनपुट डिवाइसेस से डेटा प्राप्त करता है, उसे प्रोसेस करता है, और आउटपुट डिवाइसेस को रिजल्ट भेजता है। मॉनिटर एक आउटपुट डिवाइस है, यूपीएस पावर बैकअप सिस्टम है, और एएलयू सीपीयू का एक भाग मात्र है।

Extra Facts:
सीपीयू के प्रदर्शन को क्लॉक स्पीड (हर्ट्ज़ में) से मापा जाता है। आधुनिक सीपीयू मल्टी-कोर प्रोसेसर (डुअल-कोर, क्वाड-कोर) होते हैं जो एक साथ कई टास्क्स पर काम कर सकते हैं। इंटेल और एएमडी प्रमुख सीपीयू निर्माता कंपनियाँ हैं। सीपीयू मशीन साइकिल (फ़ेच, डिकोड, एक्ज़िक्यूट, स्टोर) के माध्यम से इंस्ट्रक्शन्स प्रोसेस करता है। कैश मेमोरी सीपीयू के अंदर होती है जो डेटा एक्सेस की स्पीड बढ़ाती है। सीपीयू का विकास जनरेशन्स (पहली से पाँचवीं) में हुआ है।
